column3: The line is difficult (“who gnaw the dry ground, yesterday of ruin”); NKJV renders “Fleeing late to the wilderness, desolate and waste.”
Close to the Hebrew; “sons of no name” is rendered “sons of vile men.”
Close to the Hebrew; יִתְרִי (“my cord”) is rendered “my bowstring,” and “the bridle” “restraint.”
Close to the Hebrew; פִּרְחַח (“a brood”) is rendered “the rabble.”
Close to the Hebrew; “they profit [toward] my destruction” is rendered “They promote my calamity.”
Close to the Hebrew; “as through a wide breach” is rendered “as broad breakers,” and “devastation” “the ruinous storm.”
Close to the Hebrew; “poured out upon me” is rendered “poured out because of my plight.”
Close to the Hebrew; יִתְחַפֵּשׂ (“is disfigured”) is rendered “is disfigured.”
The Hebrew is obscure; NKJV renders “Surely He would not stretch out His hand against a heap of ruins, If they cry out when He destroys it,” supplying God as subject.
Close to the Hebrew; קֹדֵר (“darkened, in mourning”) is rendered “mourning.”
Close to the Hebrew; “daughters of the ostrich” is rendered “ostriches.”
Close to the Hebrew; “from upon me” is rendered “falls from me,” and “heat” “fever.”
